\[
(a+b+c)^2=9 \implies ab+bc+ca=\frac{9-4}{2}=\frac52.
\]
Also \(a^2+b^2+c^2=4\), so \(a^2+b^2=4-c^2\). Therefore
\[
\frac{a^2+b^2}{2-c}
= \frac{4-c^2}{2-c}
= 2+c.
\]
Applying this cyclically,
\[
\frac{a^2+b^2}{2-c}+\frac{b^2+c^2}{2-a}+\frac{c^2+a^2}{2-b}
= (2+c)+(2+a)+(2+b)
=6+(a+b+c)=9.
\]
\[
\boxed{9}
\]
